I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life, and my father before me. The soil here is good flat ground on the North China Plain. I have about 12 mu. There's really only one system that makes sense here — winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same ground. Everyone does it, and I know it works. I don't experiment with vegetables or other crops because I don't have the connections to sell them reliably, and the grain station takes everything.

For wheat, I'll plant in mid-October after rotary-tilling the maize stalks under. I'll use an improved variety — probably 济麦22 or whatever the village supply co-op has this year — not the old traditional seed, that yields too low, but I won't spend extra on the expensive hybrids either. I'll put down compound fertilizer as a base before planting, then top-dress with urea at the jointing stage in April. I need to irrigate at least three times: once before winter sets in to help root establishment, once at jointing, once at heading. If March is dry I might add a fourth. I'll spray herbicide in November or December and fungicide once in spring for rust.

After wheat harvest in early June, I'll direct-seed hybrid maize the same week — no time to plow, and the soil is already worked. I use郑单958 or 先玉335, hybrid, because that's just standard now. Summer rains cover most of the water needs but I'll irrigate twice if the monsoon is late or weak. One herbicide pass early, one spray for corn borer mid-season.
